topic: Closing your oldest credit card vs keeping it open at zero balance (Sofia vs Demi)

scenes.narration: She paid off her oldest card and closed it on a Friday. By Monday her score had dropped eighty four points. I am Doctor Dollar. Today's patient checkup starts here.
scenes.image_prompt: kids graphic novel page panel, illustrated comic book art, bold flat colors clean black ink lines, cartoon woman named doctor dollar, dark curly hair, round gold-rim glasses, kind smile, white doctor coat over teal scrubs, golden stethoscope shaped like a dollar sign, holding a clipboard with a credit-score chart, doctor dollar in a doctor's office holding a clipboard with a credit score chart falling sharply, comic burst banner reads EIGHTY FOUR POINT DROP, kids comic book illustration

scenes.narration: Sofia and Demi are both thirty four years old, both have a fifteen year old credit card, and both finally paid off their balance to zero this month.
scenes.image_prompt: kids graphic novel page panel, illustrated comic book art, bold flat colors clean black ink lines, split panel, left side woman sofia at a clinic desk with a paid card, right side woman demi with the same paid card, both with PAID OFF stamps, kids comic book illustration

scenes.narration: Sofia closes the card the same day to remove the temptation. The fifteen year history vanishes from her average account age and her credit limit drops by ten thousand dollars.
scenes.image_prompt: kids graphic novel page panel, illustrated comic book art, bold flat colors clean black ink lines, woman sofia holding scissors over a credit card, a clock behind her resetting to zero, a credit limit gauge dropping by TEN THOUSAND, kids comic book illustration

scenes.narration: Demi keeps the card open, sets a five dollar Netflix charge to autopay on it every month, and sets the card to autopay in full from her checking account.
scenes.image_prompt: kids graphic novel page panel, illustrated comic book art, bold flat colors clean black ink lines, woman demi at a kitchen table with a phone showing a NETFLIX FIVE DOLLAR autopay and a card with AUTOPAY IN FULL toggled on, kids comic book illustration

scenes.narration: Three weeks later Sofia's score drops eighty four points because her oldest account closed and her utilization on her remaining cards jumped from twelve percent to forty four.
scenes.image_prompt: kids graphic novel page panel, illustrated comic book art, bold flat colors clean black ink lines, shocked woman sofia at a kitchen table looking at a phone showing a credit score chart falling, comic banner reads EIGHTY FOUR POINTS GONE, kids comic book illustration

scenes.narration: Demi's score went up nine points. Same payoff, same month, two completely different scores from one closed card.
scenes.image_prompt: kids graphic novel page panel, illustrated comic book art, bold flat colors clean black ink lines, split scene, left side sofia staring at a falling score chart, right side demi smiling at a phone showing a score chart up by NINE POINTS, kids comic book illustration

scenes.narration: When you pay off a card, do not close it. Keep it open with one tiny autopay charge and pay it in full each month. Length of credit history is fifteen percent of your score. See you next visit. Stay financially healthy!
